avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin/Anticoagulants
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit platelet function and displace anticoagulants from protein binding, significantly increasing bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consult prescriber for alternative pain management

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive antiplatelet effects increase bleeding and bruising risk
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin E to ≤400 IU daily; monitor for signs of bleeding

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo Biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates antiplatelet effects and increases bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue ginkgo or avoid ibuprofen; consider alternative NSAID status with prescriber

caution_supplements.name: Garlic (high-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet effects may add to NSAID's platelet inhibition
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for unusual bruising or bleeding; use culinary amounts only

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet activity; CYP2C9 substrate competition possible
caution_supplements.action: Use standard doses; monitor for GI upset which may be potentiated

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil (>3g daily)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet effects; potential additive GI irritation
caution_supplements.action: Limit to ≤3g daily combined EPA/DHA; monitor for bleeding signs

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol (>2 drinks daily)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Increases GI irritation, ulceration risk, and hepatotoxicity; synergistic NSAID GI toxicity
avoid_foods.action: Minimize alcohol consumption; avoid regular concurrent use

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: Delays ibuprofen absorption and may increase GI irritation risk
caution_foods.action: Take ibuprofen with food to reduce gastric upset, but avoid high-fat meals immediately before/after

caution_foods.name: Caffeine
caution_foods.mechanism: May slightly enhance analgesia but increases GI irritation potential
caution_foods.action: Moderate caffeine intake (≤200mg daily); monitor for GI symptoms

caution_foods.name: Spicy foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase gastric irritation when combined with NSAIDs
caution_foods.action: Limit spicy foods during ibuprofen therapy; take with plain food or milk

monitoring_notes: Monitor for GI symptoms (heartburn, nausea, abdominal pain), signs of bleeding/bruising, and renal/hepatic function with prolonged use. Counsel patients to report any unusual bleeding, severe abdominal pain, or edema, especially if on concurrent anticoagulants or with renal/cardiac comorbidities.
